newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.02 pct in commercial market.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.02 pct in commercial market.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.02 percent to close at 1.0626 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market following the Central Bank's lowering of the reais-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
The Central Bank surprised the market by depreciating the mini-band for the second consecutive trading day, having done so on Friday. Monday was a local holiday.
The Central Bank Tuesday lowered the mini-band 0.09 percent to between 1.0625 and 1.0675 reais per dollar.
So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.52 percent against the dollar compared to an average drop of between 0.5 and 0.6 percent over the past four months.
The market had been expecting a 0.6 percent decline the mini-band this month, but some dealers speculated it could fall further given today's Central Bank move.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.07 percent to end at 1.0672 per greenback.
In the parallel market, the real rose 0.44 percent to close at 1.130 per dollar, traders said.
